classification.difficultyReason: Coordinate volume modelling, a tangent calculation, repeated-root and known-root cubic products, then a secant construction to obtain a new rational point and interpret its positive coordinates as radii.

inlines.text: cm. The goal is to find two
cm with the same total volume.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Show that $x^3+y^3=35$. The graph is given below.

spec.sourceRegion: Left column, below part 72(a) and above part 72(b).
spec.description: Unshaded axes with positive arrowheads, an equation-driven decreasing curve, a descending tangent and black points labelled P and (2,3). No ticks or origin label.
spec.mathematics: Curve x^3+y^3=35; tangent through (2,3) and P. P is in the second quadrant. Internal coordinates define the supplied geometry but are not printed as answers.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the source labels x, y, P and (2,3) are visible. The tangent equation and coordinates of P are hidden.

answer.short: $x^3+y^3=35$, since the common volume factor $\frac43\pi$ cancels.
answer.worked:
Equate the total volumes.
$$\begin{align*}
\frac43\pi x^3+\frac43\pi y^3&=\frac43\pi(2^3)+\frac43\pi(3^3)\\
x^3+y^3&=8+27\\
x^3+y^3&=35.
\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find the equation of the tangent at $(2,3)$.

answer.short:
$y=-\frac49x+\frac{35}{9}$.

Differentiate the curve to find the gradient at $(2,3)$.
answer.worked:
Write $y=(35-x^3)^{1/3}$ and differentiate.
$$\begin{align*}
y'&=-x^2(35-x^3)^{-2/3}\\
m&=-2^2(35-2^3)^{-2/3}\\
m&=-\frac49.
\end{align*}$$
The tangent passes through $(2,3)$.
$$\begin{align*}
y-3&=-\frac49(x-2)\\
y&=-\frac49x+\frac{35}{9}.
\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: Find the other point of intersection $P$ of this tangent with the curve. Give the coordinates as exact values.

answer.short:
$P=\left(-\frac{124}{19},\frac{129}{19}\right)$.

Substitute the tangent into the curve and use the product of roots, with $x=2$ a double root.
answer.worked:
Substitute the tangent into $x^3+y^3=35$.
$$\begin{align*}
x^3+\left(\frac{35-4x}{9}\right)^3&=35\\
729x^3+(35-4x)^3-25515&=0.
\end{align*}$$
The leading coefficient is $729-64=665$ and the constant term is $35^3-25515=17360$. Tangency gives a double root at $x=2$. Let the remaining root be $p$.
$$\begin{align*}
(2)(2)p&=-\frac{17360}{665}\\
p&=-\frac{17360}{4(665)}\\
p&=-\frac{124}{19}.
\end{align*}$$
Substitute into the tangent.
$$\begin{align*}
y_P&=-\frac49\left(-\frac{124}{19}\right)+\frac{35}{9}\\
y_P&=\frac{129}{19}.
\end{align*}$$
Hence $P=\left(-\frac{124}{19},\frac{129}{19}\right)$.

children.label: d
children.prompt: Find the remaining point of intersection of the line passing through $P$ and $(3,2)$ with the curve. Hence, deduce the rational radii of differently sized spheres with the same total volume as the original two spheres.

answer.short:
Remaining intersection: $\left(\frac{8693}{18162},\frac{59347}{18162}\right)$.

The radii are $\frac{8693}{18162}$ cm and $\frac{59347}{18162}$ cm. Use the product of roots after substituting the secant into the curve.
answer.worked:
The gradient of the line through $P$ and $(3,2)$ is
$$\begin{align*}
m&=\frac{2-\frac{129}{19}}{3+\frac{124}{19}}\\
m&=-\frac{91}{181}.
\end{align*}$$
Using $(3,2)$ gives
$$\begin{align*}
y-2&=-\frac{91}{181}(x-3)\\
y&=\frac{635-91x}{181}.
\end{align*}$$
Substitute into the curve.
$$\begin{align*}
x^3+\left(\frac{635-91x}{181}\right)^3&=35\\
181^3x^3+(635-91x)^3-35(181^3)&=0.
\end{align*}$$
The leading coefficient is $181^3-91^3=5176170$ and the constant term is $635^3-35(181^3)=48506940$. Two roots are $-\frac{124}{19}$ and $3$. Let the third root be $r$.
$$\begin{align*}
\left(-\frac{124}{19}\right)(3)r&=-\frac{48506940}{5176170}\\
r&=\frac{48506940\cdot19}{5176170\cdot372}\\
r&=\frac{8693}{18162}.
\end{align*}$$
Its corresponding ordinate is
$$\begin{align*}
y&=\frac{635-91\left(\frac{8693}{18162}\right)}{181}\\
y&=\frac{59347}{18162}.
\end{align*}$$
The remaining intersection is $\left(\frac{8693}{18162},\frac{59347}{18162}\right)$. Both coordinates are positive and different, so the required radii are $\frac{8693}{18162}$ cm and $\frac{59347}{18162}$ cm.
